texts.facts: A Claim Petition was preferred under Section 166 and 140 of Motor Vehicle Act on 28.11.2017 for grant of compensation of Rs.25 lakhs by Sh. Avinash Bhadauria (hereinafter called the claimant) against Sh. Bhahampal (hereinafter called the driver/respondent no.1), Sh. Ram Kumar (hereinafter called the owner/respondent no.2) and The National Insurance Company Ltd. (hereinafter called the insurer/respondent no.3) in respect of injuries sustained by him in an accident which took place on 04.06.2016 at about 08:50 PM on Karnal-Shamli-Meerut Road, near Police Post after Yamuna bridge, toward Uttar Pradesh within the jurisdiction of PS Jhinjhana, District Shamli, Uttar Pradesh, allegedly caused due to rash and negligent driving of Bajaj Platina Motorcycle bearing Registration no. HR-02U/2017 (hereinafter referred as offending vehicle). 2. It is averred in the petition that on 04.06.2016 at about 08:50 PM, while claimant was crossing the road, he got hit by the offending vehicle, being driven in high speed in a casual and MACT No. 930/2017 Avinash Bhadauriya Vs. Braham Pal & Ors. page no.2 of 31 negligent manner. It is also stated therein that two pillion riders were seated on the motor cycle which made it difficult for the driver to control which is why it got rammed into the legs of claimant fracturing his left femur bone. It is stated that the police was informed immediately and claimant being injured was rushed to hospital in an ambulance. FIR was registered. The offending vehicle was seized by the police persons and respondent no.1 was arrested. It is also stated that medical bill of sum of Rs.1,32,545/- was reimbursed towards the treatment cost by insurer by the claimant. It is stated that the claimant could not attend to his work for a long time because of the accident. It is stated that responsibility of payment of compensation must be fastened on all the respondents and compensation of Rs.25 lakhs should be awarded in his favour. 3. Upon receipt of claim petition, notice was directed to be issued to respondents, in response to which counsel for respondent no.1 and 3 appeared. 4. In the written statement filed on behalf of R1, contradiction has been highlighted in respect to the reason for claimant to cross the road to go the other side after parking his car on one side of the road, as mentioned in the FIR in contrast to what has been stated in the claim petition. It is stated that the offending vehicle was not involved in any accident. Other assertions made in the claim petition were also denied. 5. No written statement was filed by R2. R2 was proceeded against ex-parte vide order dated 20.05.2019. 6. Insurance company / R3 did not file any reply. Thus, their MACT No. 930/2017 Avinash Bhadauriya Vs. Braham Pal & Ors. page no.3 of 31 right to file the same was closed vide order dated Avinash Bhadauria vs Braham Pal on 1 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/10514899/ 2 15.07.2019. 7. An application for assessment of physical disability by Medical Board was filed and allowed, as per which permanent disability has been assessed to be 13% in relation to left lower limb. 8. From the pleadings of parties, following issues were framed by Ld. Predecessor of this Tribunal vide order dated 15.07.2019 : i). Whether the injured suffered injuries in a road traffic accident on 04.06.2016 due to rash and negligent driving of vehicle no. HR-02U/2017 being driven R1, owned by R2 and insured with R3? OPP iii). Relief. 9. Thereafter matter was listed for recording of evidence. 10. On 26.02.2024, claimant appeared as PW-1 and tendered his evidentiary affidavit Ex.PW1/1 and also relied upon his proof of official address of the petition I- card, letter of appointment as Ex.PW1/A, certified copy of FIR as Ex.PW1/B, certified copy of charge sheet as Ex.PW1/C, certified copy of Naksha Nazri as Ex.PW1/D, photocopy of RC of offending vehicle as Ex.PW1/E, copy of insurance police as Ex.PW1/F, copy of driving license of R1 as Ex.PW1/G, copy of insurance police of the petitioner as Ex.PW1/H, copy of ITR of the petition as Ex.PW1/J, copy of hospital paper/discharge summary as Ex.PW1/K, original MACT No. 930/2017 Avinash Bhadauriya Vs. Braham Pal & Ors. page no.4 of 31 medical bills as Ex.PW1/L and photocopy of Aadhar card & PAN Card of the petitioner as Ex.PW1/M. 11. No other evidence has been led on behalf of petitioner and PE was closed on 26.02.2024. Thereafter, matter was listed for RE, however, RE was not led on behalf of any of the respondents and therefore, RE was closed vide order dated 26.02.2024. 12. Arguments in detail were addressed by counsels for petitioner, Respondent No.1 as well as Insurance Company. Counsel for claimant has argued that claimant had to suffer on account of irresponsible driving of R1, who was driving the bike without any regard for the applicable traffic rules for which he deserve to compensate him.

Therefore, in my opinion, there cannot be any hard and fast rule in awarding interest and the award of interest is solely on the discretion of the Tribunal of the High Court as indicated above."
